text:
alex: ran a focused nsys + perfetto capture on the KV cache alloc path during a 2k-token steady workload. attaching links to traces: https://perf.company/trace/1799998888 and quick nvprof output.
maria: saw it too - spikes line up with cache cold-fill bursts. cudaMalloc spikes every ~150ms when multiple sessions warm up and evict at the same time. looks like allocator churn, not kernel compute.
jordan: quick excerpt from the perfetto timeline:
```
00:00.000 cuMemAlloc 1.9ms (KVCache::grow)
00:00.002 attention_fwd 0.7ms
00:00.003 cuMemAlloc 2.1ms (KVCache::grow)
00:00.005 attention_bwd 0.9ms
...
```
That pattern repeats in bursts and aligns with batching spikes.
sam: nvtx ranges show the allocator call sits on the critical path during prefix cache fill. Batching heuristic currently allows many micro-batches to race and all request a new chunk simultaneously.
dina: perf-bot posted aggregated stats: `perf-bot: 1799998888: cudaMalloc count +23% vs baseline, avg latency +1.8ms/alloc, 95p latency 3.4ms` — this matches our nsys sample.
alex: hypothesis: our arena growth policy is too eager at boundary conditions. when an arena is nearly full we create a new arena which triggers repeated large allocations for small KV pages; fragmentation + CUDA allocator overhead = spike.
maria: also noticed free list reuse is not happening because page sizes vary (we use power-of-two rounding) and small evictions create many small free extents mixed with large ones -> fragmentation.
jordan: experiments I ran locally:
- change slab growth_factor from 2.0 -> 1.25: reduces large sudden allocations but increases number of arenas slightly
- pre-reserve 256MB warm slab per GPU at startup: eliminates first-minute spike entirely
sam: can we instrument the KVCache allocation hot path with a simple counter + NVTX around alloc/free and a histogram of requested sizes? we need to know request-size distribution during multi-tenant bursts.
dina: already added a light-weight counter in a branch: https://git.company/repo/kvcache/alloc-sampling. gathered histo for a 5m run: top bins: 4KB(42%), 64KB(28%), 1MB(12%), >8MB(3%).
alex: so 4KB & 64KB are most common. cudaMalloc at that granularity is dangerous. we should switch small-size requests to a subpage allocator inside arena: keep big-page allocations for >512KB only.
maria: suggestion: implement a per-GPU slab allocator with fixed-size buckets for {4KB, 16KB, 64KB, 256KB} and fallback to arena for larger. This avoids cudaMalloc for the common case.
jordan: +1. Also change batching heuristic: add a per-model jitter window (10-30ms) to smooth concurrent cache-fills across requests, and add a small cooperative backoff when cache-fill is detected to prevent thundering herd.
sam: i'll prototype the slab buckets and add histogram-based thresholds. plan:
1) add NVTX around bucket alloc/free and track misses to arena
2) pre-alloc N pages per bucket at startup (configurable via REDWOOD_KVCACHE_SLAB_PREALLOC)
3) fallback to arena (cudaMalloc) only when slab exhausted
alex: perf expectations: reduce cudaMalloc count by ~60-80% on steady traffic, cut alloc latency out of critical path, smooth P95 token latency. also reduces fragmentation so arena growth rate will slow.
dina: perf-bot summary after a 30m canary run on dev cluster: `cudaMalloc cnt -72%`, `avg latency -0.9ms`, `P95 token latency -11%`. traces show far fewer cuMemAlloc events in perfetto.
maria: edge cases: background GC/free coalescing still needed. implement deferred coalescing to avoid synchronous work during request handling. also add a background thread to compact low-util arenas.
jordan: regression guard: add an eval flow that stresses KV cache warmups across 50 concurrent sessions and asserts cudaMalloc count decrease and P95 latency not worse than baseline.
sam: i'll send a PR with the slab bucket prototype + NVTX metrics. tagging @dina for perf dashboards and @maria for arena coalescer design review. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: Capture saved at https://perf.company/trace/1799998888, summary metrics uploaded to https://dash.company/kvcache/1799998888

alex: thanks team — let's aim to land prototype behind a feature flag and run a two-day canary on dedicated cluster. if numbers hold we'll flip for Dedicated and opt-in Hosted tiers first.
